display.title: Pinhere issue collaboration API
display.summary: Pinhere APIs for projects, origins, issues, private screenshots, webhooks, PATs, and Chrome-extension OAuth. The fixed PontxSpec covers all 34 Endpoints. Hub provides documentation and a local SDK/CLI only; it proxies no request.

documentation.stabilityNote: The contract is Pinhere's product-owned PontxSpec at a fixed revision. Every Endpoint either reads private project or issue data or makes a persistent change. Attachments, session cookies, PATs, Webhook secrets, OAuth values, and screenshots must never be sent to, stored by, or logged by Hub. Requests originate only in the caller's locally controlled SDK or CLI process with caller-owned credentials.

pricing.summary: No public pricing commitment has been verified from an immutable official source. Confirm the current Pinhere product page or account agreement before integrating.

credentials.description: A caller-owned Pinhere PAT is sent through a Bearer header and retained only in a locally controlled environment. Never place it in Hub, logs, examples, or chat.

guide.title: Create a Pinhere PAT
steps: Sign in to the Pinhere website and open API Token management.
Create a PAT. Its plaintext is shown only once, so save it immediately in controlled local secret storage.
Set PINHERE_ACCESS_TOKEN only in the local SDK/CLI. Never send it to Hub, logs, examples, or chat.

credentials.description: A website Session Cookie is limited to the caller's authenticated same-origin context. Never copy it into Hub, CLI history, logs, or examples.

guide.title: Use a Pinhere website session
steps: Sign in on the official Pinhere website and let the browser manage the Session Cookie on same-origin pages.
A website session is only for authenticated same-origin browser requests; it is not a distributable API credential.
Do not inspect, copy, or paste the Cookie into Hub, CLI history, logs, or examples. Use a PAT for automation.

credentials.description: The Chrome extension uses OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE. Its short-lived Bearer access token may be supplied locally as PINHERE_ACCESS_TOKEN; authorization codes, refresh tokens, and code verifiers stay within the caller's extension and server.

guide.title: Authorize the Pinhere Chrome extension
steps: Sign in to the Pinhere website, then start authorization from the Pinhere Chrome extension.
Confirm the extension and callback on the authorization page; the extension exchanges the PKCE code for a short-lived access token.
Let the extension manage its access token, refresh token, and code verifier. Never copy them into Hub or logs.
